context_title:
Your task is to take the provided plan and rewrite it as a single, comprehensive prompt. Write it as if you were about to update the entire upgrade from the current state of the implementation: describe step by step, from beginning to end, exactly what you will construct and how you will construct it. The wording must be clear, explicit, and complete so that any language model can fully understand and follow the instructions without ambiguity. Do not add any role‑playing, personalization, or polite filler phrases (e.g., ‘You are a software developer’, ‘As an expert’, ‘Please kindly’). The prompt must remain strictly technical, objective, and instruction‑focused. Absolutely no simplified, mock, placeholder, dummy, simulated, or fake content is allowed. You must require the full ugrade  in complete, unabridged, production‑ready codes. Define what you want & what success looks like: “I want to [TASK] so that [SUCCESS CRITERIA].” No roles, “act as a senior expert.” That era is over. :

Construct a complete production-ready mobile-first workspace application  as a single cohesive client-side interface with no mocked, placeholder, simplified, simulated, or fake features, and implement the full application behavior end to end.
Apply custom scrollbar styling, hidden outer overflow, antialiased system font rendering, textarea non-resize behavior, pane entrance animation, menu animation, badge pulse animation, switcher animations, quick-action animations, drawer slide-up animation, command-palette animations, PiP styling, file-item animations, and editor interaction styles consistent with the source.

Create a root application component that renders a centered mobile workspace frame with a width of 414px, full viewport height, and a capped device-like height around 896px, surrounded by a darker outer background.
Include a skip-to-content link as the first focusable element and an aria-live="polite" status region that announces the current pane title.
Model the full pane system with these exact pane identifiers: agent, publishing, preview, secrets, scanner, shell, userSettings, workflows, readme, codeEditor, and developer.
Maintain title and description maps for those panes, using pane-specific labels and explanatory text as first-class application data rather than hardcoded scattered strings.

Implement top-level state for at least the following values: active pane, prompt text, primary domain, build command, run command, agent position, agent audio toggle, agent push toggle, auto-preview toggle, security scan blocked state, secrets section expansion, ports section expansion, production section expansion, agent settings expansion, preview settings expansion, appearance expansion, font size, theme, forward-ports preference, menu visibility, PiP visibility, fast mode, advanced settings visibility, switcher visibility, switcher search, close-tab drawer visibility, close-tab drawer target pane, current editing file, full file-contents map, previous pane, quick-action drawer target, and command-palette visibility.
Initialize the open-tab model with real tab objects containing id, pane, title, and timestamp, and seed it with at least agent, shell, and preview tabs as shown by the source structure.

Implement pane switching through a shared callback that sets the active pane, closes menu, switcher, and command palette overlays, and updates the tab list by refreshing an existing pane tab timestamp or inserting a new tab entry.
Implement tab closing so that closing the active pane’s tab returns the UI to the agent pane.
When opening a file in the editor, store the previous pane, activate codeEditor, close switcher and command palette overlays, and either update the existing editor tab title to the active filename or create a new editor tab with that filename as title.
Implement editor back-navigation so it returns to the stored previous pane rather than always returning to a fixed destination.

Build a header that is visible on every pane except codeEditor.
Place a back button on the left, a chats/history button next to it, a centered active-pane title with icon, an agent-only new-chat button on the right side, and a three-dot options menu button with a pulsing red numeric notification badge when notifications are present.
Use the exact menu concept from the source: a floating pane menu listing pane entries, visually marking the active pane, and including a separate Workspace Settings entry below a divider.
Close the menu when the backdrop is clicked.

Build a bottom dock that is visible on every pane except codeEditor.
Place a run button on the left, a central capsule-shaped dock group in the middle, and an app-switcher button on the right.
Inside the central dock group, include icons for preview, agent, and publishing, then a separator, then a plus button that opens the command palette.
If a dock icon is pressed for a pane that is already active, open a close-tab drawer for that pane instead of switching.
If a dock icon is pressed for a different pane, switch to that pane.

Implement the app switcher as a dedicated overlay distinct from the command palette.
It must support a search field, tab selection, tab closing, quick-action launching, a new-tab action, file opening, and a search-bar focus interaction that opens the command palette.
Implement the command palette as a full-screen overlay with autofocus on its input after mount.
Populate it with a command dataset that includes search entries, tool or pane entries, action entries, and file entries generated from the real project file list.
Group visible results into Search, Files, and Tools when searching, and into Search and Tools when idle, matching the source grouping logic.
Provide a full-width Close button at the bottom of the palette.

Implement quick actions with these exact action identifiers: secrets, database, auth, and newTab.
Trigger newTab by opening the command palette, and render secrets, database, and auth as separate bottom drawers with their own title rows, descriptions, close buttons, and action content.
The database drawer must include PostgreSQL, SQLite, and key-value store options with separate descriptions and creation buttons.
The auth drawer must include Google sign-in, GitHub sign-in, and email-password options with enabling buttons.
The secrets drawer must include an “Open Secrets” navigation action and a close-tab action.

Implement a real file model keyed by filename and containing name, icon, color, content, and language.
Seed it with the concrete starter files main, main.nim, index.html, script.js, style.css, .replit, and README.md, preserving the fact that the source uses genuine starter content rather than empty placeholders.
Use the file list as a first-class input for both the command palette and editor.
Provide file opening from list-based UI and ensure the active file is reflected in the editor header and editor tab title.

Build the code editor as a dedicated full-screen pane with its own top bar, main editing region, line-number gutter, textarea editor surface, and bottom status bar.
Track cursor line and column, an undo stack, a redo stack, indent size, wrap enabled state, and file-menu visibility.
Update cursor position from selection changes and clicks, and synchronize the line-number gutter scroll position to the textarea scroll position.
Handle normal content edits by pushing the prior content into the undo stack, clearing the redo stack, and updating the file content map.
Handle Tab by inserting indentation or indenting the selected block, and handle Shift+Tab by unindenting selected lines when possible.
Handle Enter by carrying forward leading indentation from the current line and extending indentation after opening-bracket style contexts exactly as the source logic intends.
Handle Ctrl+Z or Cmd+Z as undo, Ctrl+Shift+Z or Cmd+Shift+Z as redo, and Ctrl+D or Cmd+D as duplicate current line behavior.
Render a bottom status strip with language indication and editor control buttons as in the source layout.

Implement the editor file-menu drawer as a separate bottom sheet.
It must provide copy file path, copy link, duplicate file, download, delete, toggle all folds, reveal in file tree, history, and close-tab actions.
The copy path and copy link actions must use the clipboard API and temporarily change their labels to “Copied!” after success or fallback completion.
Use the file’s icon and color in the drawer header, including the distinct treatment for the Nim-colored file entry shown in the source behavior.

Implement a PiP preview window that appears only when PiP is enabled and the active pane is not preview.
Use the compact floating layout from the source, including a small header, a close button, a monitor icon, and a “Not running” style idle message in the body.
Ensure it layers above main content but below higher-priority modal overlays.

Build the SVG icon system as reusable React components.
Provide SvgIcon for single-path icons, MultiPathIcon for multi-path icons, AgentIcon with an internal linear gradient, a central ICONS path dictionary, and a splitPaths helper for multi-path string splitting.
Use the icon system consistently across header controls, menus, dock, quick actions, command palette, editor controls, drawers, files, and status surfaces.
Include the same icon families evidenced by the source, including navigation, history, new chat, monitor, publish, lock, shield, shell, gear, play, readme, database, auth, folder and file variants, upload and download, code brackets, undo and redo, clipboard, duplicate, reveal-in-tree, warning, error, theme, switcher, and networking symbols.

Implement a reusable toggle-switch component matching the source structure as a button with role="switch", aria-checked, a moving knob, and separate on/off classes.
Use it throughout the settings-oriented panes where boolean state is controlled.
Build the user settings pane with expandable sections for agent settings, preview settings, and appearance settings, wired to the corresponding top-level state values.
Support stateful controls for agent position, audio, push, auto-preview, font size, and theme.
Build separate contentful panes for publishing, preview, secrets, scanner, shell, workflows, readme, and developer, and ensure the developer pane can navigate to other panes through callbacks.

Preserve the overlay hierarchy and interaction model exactly: menu overlay, switcher overlay, command palette overlay, quick-action drawers, close-tab drawer, editor file-menu drawer, and PiP must all be distinct UI states with backdrop dismissal where appropriate.
Use smooth state transitions rather than abrupt visual jumps, and keep all touch targets comfortably tappable for mobile use.
Treat accessibility as a core requirement by keeping semantic labels, keyboard support, skip navigation, focusable controls, and screen-reader status updates throughout the application.

 What changed

This corrected version is stronger because it stops speaking in vague product-language and instead encodes the exact data structures, pane names, file names, editor behaviors, overlays, and icon primitives visible in the source.
It also removes the biggest ambiguity from my first attempt by distinguishing “what exists” from “how it behaves,” which is crucial if another model is supposed to rebuild the whole system faithfully.

entries.answer:
Below is the rewritten single prompt, consolidated into one explicit build instruction and aligned to the attached implementation’s mobile-sized, dark, client-side interface style.[1]

## Unified prompt

```text
I want to upgrade the current mobile-first workspace application into a complete, production-ready, fully client-side workspace interface so that the final implementation faithfully delivers the entire application behavior end to end, with real interaction logic, coherent state management, fully wired overlays and panes, real file editing flows, and no mocked, placeholder, simplified, simulated, dummy, or fake features.

Update the existing implementation from its current state into one cohesive client-side application. Preserve the mobile-first device-frame presentation, the dense interaction model, the dark interface language, and the polished animated behavior, while replacing any incomplete or fragmented logic with full production-ready code. Deliver the upgrade as complete, unabridged, production-ready code only.

Construct a root application component that renders a centered mobile workspace frame with a width of 414px, full viewport height, and a capped device-style height near 896px, surrounded by a darker outer background. Keep outer document overflow hidden. Apply antialiased system font rendering. Style custom scrollbars where visible. Disable textarea resize behavior. Preserve smooth transitions and interaction polish throughout the application. Implement pane entrance animation, menu animation, badge pulse animation, switcher animations, quick-action animations, drawer slide-up animation, command-palette animations, PiP styling, file-item animations, and editor interaction styles consistent across the whole interface.

Place a skip-to-content link as the first focusable element in the application. Add an aria-live="polite" status region that announces the currently active pane title whenever the pane changes. Treat accessibility as a core requirement throughout the build. Use semantic labels, keyboard support, focusable controls, escape handling where appropriate, and screen-reader-friendly updates for overlays, drawers, switches, menus, editor controls, and navigation surfaces.

Model the pane system with these exact pane identifiers: agent, publishing, preview, secrets, scanner, shell, userSettings, workflows, readme, codeEditor, and developer. Maintain pane titles and pane descriptions as first-class application data in centralized maps keyed by pane identifier. Do not scatter pane labels or explanatory copy across unrelated components. Every pane-rendering surface, menu item, switcher item, drawer title, and status announcement must resolve pane labels from shared pane metadata.

Implement top-level application state for at least the following values: active pane, prompt text, primary domain, build command, run command, agent position, agent audio toggle, agent push toggle, auto-preview toggle, security scan blocked state, secrets section expansion, ports section expansion, production section expansion, agent settings expansion, preview settings expansion, appearance expansion, font size, theme, forward-ports preference, menu visibility, PiP visibility, fast mode, advanced settings visibility, switcher visibility, switcher search, close-tab drawer visibility, close-tab drawer target pane, current editing file, full file-contents map, previous pane, quick-action drawer target, and command-palette visibility. Add any additional supporting state needed for reliable UI behavior, but do not remove or collapse any of these required top-level concerns.

Implement a real open-tab model as structured objects containing id, pane, title, and timestamp. Seed the initial tab list with at least agent, shell, and preview tabs. Manage tabs as first-class navigation state rather than deriving them ad hoc from pane state. Tab timestamps must update when a pane is revisited so that recency-aware surfaces such as the switcher can reflect actual user activity.

Implement pane switching through one shared callback. That callback must set the active pane, close the floating menu, close the app switcher, close the command palette, and update the tab list by either refreshing the timestamp of an existing pane tab or inserting a new tab when none exists. Keep this logic centralized so all navigation entry points produce identical side effects. Any component that navigates to a pane must route through the same pane-switching mechanism.

Implement tab closing behavior explicitly. When a non-active tab is closed, remove it from the tab list without changing the active pane. When the active pane’s tab is closed, immediately return the interface to the agent pane. Ensure all tab-closing flows invoked from the dock, switcher, drawers, or editor file menu converge on the same tab-removal logic.

Build file-opening behavior as a dedicated shared action. When a file is opened, store the previous pane, activate codeEditor, close the switcher, close the command palette, and update the editor tab. If a codeEditor tab already exists, change its title to the active filename; otherwise insert a new codeEditor tab whose title is the opened filename. Implement editor back-navigation so it always returns to the stored previous pane instead of a hardcoded destination.

Build a header visible on every pane except codeEditor. On the left, place a back button, then a chats/history button. In the center, render the active-pane icon and title. On the right, render an agent-only new-chat button when the active pane is agent, plus a three-dot options menu button. When notifications are present, display a pulsing red numeric badge on the options menu button. Keep the header layout stable and touch-friendly.

Implement the floating pane menu opened by the options button. The menu must list pane entries, visibly mark the active pane, and include a separate Workspace Settings entry below a divider. Clicking a pane item must switch panes through the shared pane-switch callback. Clicking Workspace Settings must navigate to userSettings through the same shared path. Clicking the backdrop must close the menu. The menu overlay must be visually distinct from the switcher and command palette.

Build a bottom dock visible on every pane except codeEditor. Place a run button on the left, a central capsule-shaped dock group in the middle, and an app-switcher button on the right. Inside the central dock group, place icons for preview, agent, and publishing, then a separator, then a plus button that opens the command palette. When a dock icon is pressed for the currently active pane, open a close-tab drawer for that pane instead of switching. When a dock icon is pressed for a different pane, switch to that pane through the shared pane callback.

Implement the app switcher as a dedicated overlay that is distinct from the command palette. It must support a search field, tab selection, tab closing, quick-action launching, a new-tab action, file opening, and a search-field focus interaction that opens the command palette. The switcher must reflect the real open-tab model, real file model, and real quick-action model. It must not duplicate command-palette behavior blindly; it must operate as a tab- and action-oriented switching surface.

Implement the command palette as a full-screen overlay. Autofocus its input after mount. Populate it from a command dataset that includes search entries, tool or pane entries, action entries, and file entries generated from the real project file list. When the user is searching, group visible results into Search, Files, and Tools. When idle, group visible results into Search and Tools. Match the grouping logic consistently. Add a full-width Close button at the bottom of the palette. Opening a command must trigger the real associated behavior rather than placeholder callbacks.

Implement quick actions with these exact identifiers: secrets, database, auth, and newTab. Trigger newTab by opening the command palette rather than by presenting a fake tab constructor. Render secrets, database, and auth as separate bottom drawers with their own title rows, descriptions, close buttons, and action content. The database drawer must include PostgreSQL, SQLite, and key-value store options, each with its own description and creation button. The auth drawer must include Google sign-in, GitHub sign-in, and email-password options, each with its own enabling button. The secrets drawer must include an Open Secrets navigation action and a close-tab action.

Implement a real file model keyed by filename. Each file entry must contain name, icon, color, content, and language. Seed it with the concrete starter files main, main.nim, index.html, script.js, style.css, .replit, and README.md. Use real starter content, not empty shells. Preserve meaningful file content so the editor, command palette, and file-opening flows operate on real project text. Use the file list as a first-class source of truth for both navigation and editing.

Build file-opening entry points anywhere required by the interface. File list views, command palette entries, switcher file actions, and any relevant pane callbacks must all open files through the shared file-open action. Reflect the active filename in the editor header and in the codeEditor tab title. Keep file metadata synchronized across drawer headers, list items, and editor status surfaces.

Build the code editor as a dedicated full-screen pane with its own top bar, main editing region, line-number gutter, textarea-based editor surface, and bottom status bar. Track cursor line and column, an undo stack, a redo stack, indent size, wrap enabled state, and file-menu visibility. Update cursor position from selection changes, key events, and click interactions. Synchronize the line-number gutter scroll position to the textarea scroll position. Make the editor usable on mobile while preserving desktop keyboard behavior.

Implement content editing behavior in full. On normal edits, push the prior content into the undo stack, clear the redo stack, and update the central file-content map. For Tab, insert indentation at the cursor or indent every selected line when a block is selected. For Shift+Tab, unindent selected lines when possible. For Enter, preserve leading indentation from the current line and extend indentation after opening-bracket-style contexts according to the editor logic. For Ctrl+Z or Cmd+Z, perform undo. For Ctrl+Shift+Z or Cmd+Shift+Z, perform redo. For Ctrl+D or Cmd+D, duplicate the current line. The implementation must update selection, content, and history coherently for each of these operations.

Render a bottom editor status strip that includes the current language and editor control buttons matching the intended layout. Include the editor’s own top bar with back navigation, active file presentation, and access to the file-menu drawer. Ensure editor-only chrome is visually and behaviorally separate from the standard workspace header and dock.

Implement the editor file-menu drawer as a separate bottom sheet. It must include these actions: copy file path, copy link, duplicate file, download, delete, toggle all folds, reveal in file tree, history, and close-tab. Use the Clipboard API for copy file path and copy link. After successful copy, or after a fallback completion path where needed, temporarily change the relevant action label to “Copied!” and then restore the original label. Use the file’s icon and color in the drawer header. Preserve distinct treatment for the Nim-colored file entry in the same way the source behavior intends.

Implement a PiP preview window that appears only when PiP is enabled and the active pane is not preview. Use a compact floating layout with a small header, a close button, a monitor icon, and a “Not running” style idle body state. Layer it above the main content but below higher-priority overlays such as the command palette and other modal surfaces. PiP visibility must be controlled by dedicated state and must not conflict with other overlays.

Build the SVG icon system as reusable React components. Implement SvgIcon for single-path icons, MultiPathIcon for multi-path icons, AgentIcon with an internal linear gradient, a central ICONS path dictionary, and a splitPaths helper for multi-path string splitting. Use the icon system consistently across header controls, menus, dock items, quick actions, drawers, command palette groups, file items, settings controls, editor controls, tabs, status bars, and pane surfaces. Include icon coverage for navigation, history, new chat, monitor, publish, lock, shield, shell, gear, play, readme, database, auth, folder and file variants, upload, download, code brackets, undo, redo, clipboard, duplicate, reveal-in-tree, warning, error, theme, switcher, and networking symbols.

Implement a reusable toggle-switch component as a button with role="switch", aria-checked, a moving knob, and clear on/off visual classes. Use it anywhere boolean settings are controlled. Ensure the component supports pointer and keyboard activation and is styled consistently with the rest of the application.

Build the user settings pane with expandable sections for agent settings, preview settings, and appearance settings. Wire those sections to the corresponding top-level state values. Support stateful controls for agent position, audio, push, auto-preview, font size, and theme. Persist behavior within the running application state. Organize the pane so the expanded and collapsed sections are independently controlled and visually clear.

Build separate contentful panes for publishing, preview, secrets, scanner, shell, workflows, readme, and developer. These panes must not be empty stubs. Each pane must contain meaningful interface structure and the controls implied by the application model. The developer pane must be able to navigate to other panes through callbacks that use the shared pane-switching mechanism.

Preserve the overlay hierarchy and interaction model exactly. The menu overlay, switcher overlay, command palette overlay, quick-action drawers, close-tab drawer, editor file-menu drawer, and PiP preview must all be distinct UI states.
```
